a.speaker: Ruth Pellow
a.text:
Ruth spent thirty-one years as a 911 dispatcher and still sits like she's waiting for the board to light. The oxygen line runs from her nose to a concentrator humming on her porch.

"If the power ever goes for more than a few hours, would you knock? The machine runs on the wall. The bottles in the closet give me two days, maybe."

options.text: "I'll knock. First thing. You have my word."
effects: Knock on Ruth's door if the power fails

options.text: "{partner.name} knows more about oxygen than I do. Let's put you on our list."
effects: Knock on Ruth's door if the power fails

options.text: "I can't promise that, Ruth. I'm not always home."

promise.speaker: Ruth Pellow
promise.text: "Good. I ran the check-on chain for this street once. Maybe I will again." She writes your house number on a card and tucks it in her blouse pocket.

decline.speaker: Ruth Pellow
decline.text: "Honest, at least." She looks back at the table. No promise, no Tally, nothing owed.
